extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigates the transferability and performance of European-derived Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS) across diverse global populations, demonstrating consistent associations with AD risk and biomarkers and improved prediction in non-European ancestries when including the APOE region, while also detailing the comprehensive methodological framework for generating these scores.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Application, evaluation, and methodological development of Alzheimer's disease polygenic risk scores (PGS/PRS)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study developed and evaluated polygenic scores (PGS) for Alzheimer's disease (AD). PGS ALZ was derived from 83 independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) excluding the APOE locus, and an APOE-inclusive PGS was also generated. Associations were assessed across various PGS ALZ strata (e.g., 0–2% vs. 98–100% relative to 40–60% reference). Cross-ancestry polygenic risk scores (PRS COMB) were constructed using the Bayesian PRS-CSx method, integrating GWAS summary statistics from European, African American, Latin American, and East Asian populations, and evaluated across different sparseness values and both with and without the APOE region. Methodological details included stringent variant quality control (e.g., R^2 < 0.3 excluded), imputation with TOPMed reference panel, ancestry determination, population structure adjustment using principal components (first 14 PCs), and clumping criteria (P-value threshold of 1 x 10^-3 and R^2 of 0.05).

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher or lower depending on stratum
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In the 0–2% PGS ALZ stratum, a greater than twofold decrease in AD risk was observed; in the 98–100% stratum, a greater than threefold increase in AD risk was observed, both compared to the 40–60% reference stratum. Association was significant in most European and diverse ancestry populations irrespective of APOE adjustment.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the genetic predisposition and probability of developing Alzheimer's disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Application of PGS ALZ in case-control studies across 17 European countries and diverse populations (Asia, Africa, Latin America, North America), with and without APOE adjustment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the genetic likelihood of developing Alzheimer's disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: PGS ALZ was associated with a younger age at onset in most populations studied. Exceptions were Chinese and Korean populations, where APOE ε2/ε3/ε4 alleles influenced age at onset.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the timing of Alzheimer's disease manifestation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Association with PGS ALZ in European and diverse ancestry populations.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts an earlier onset of Alzheimer's disease based on genetic predisposition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with a decrement in Aβ42 levels, irrespective of APOE adjustment. The lowest levels were observed in the 80–100% PGS ALZ stratum, and the highest levels in the 0–20% PGS ALZ stratum, compared to the 40–60% reference stratum.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Key component of amyloid plaques; its clearance and aggregation are central to Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Association with PGS ALZ in 13,051 individuals, with and without APOE adjustment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lower CSF Aβ42 levels are indicative of cerebral amyloidosis and increased risk for Alzheimer's disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with an increment in tau levels, irrespective of APOE adjustment.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Microtubule-associated protein; hyperphosphorylation and aggregation form neurofibrillary tangles in Alzheimer's disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Association with PGS ALZ in 13,051 individuals, with and without APOE adjustment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher CSF tau levels are indicative of neurodegeneration and increased risk for Alzheimer's disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with an increment in p-tau levels, irrespective of APOE adjustment. The highest levels were observed in the 80–100% PGS ALZ stratum, and the lowest levels in the 0–20% PGS ALZ stratum, compared to the 40–60% reference stratum.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Phosphorylated form of tau, a specific marker for neurofibrillary tangle pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Association with PGS ALZ in 13,051 individuals, with and without APOE adjustment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher CSF p-tau levels are indicative of neurofibrillary pathology and increased risk for Alzheimer's disease.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No increment in strength of association with AD risk or predictive performance relative to PGS ALZ (Supplementary Table 9).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Assessment of genetic predisposition to Alzheimer's Disease by integrating ancestry-specific SNPs into a European GWAS-defined polygenic score.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease risk assessment in multiancestry populations (Latin American, East Asian, African American) using polygenic scores.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Does not enhance genetic risk prediction for Alzheimer's Disease compared to a simple European-based PGS ALZ, despite including ancestry-specific variants.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not systematically outperform a simple PGS ALZ when the APOE locus was excluded; a singular exception in Latin American MVP population was noted with a caveat of potential overfitting.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Assessment of genetic predisposition to Alzheimer's Disease using a cross-ancestry Bayesian polygenic modeling method, excluding the APOE region.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease risk assessment in multiancestry populations using cross-ancestry Bayesian polygenic modeling, particularly considering limitations in GWAS size for diverse ancestries.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Does not consistently improve genetic risk prediction for Alzheimer's Disease compared to a simple European-based PGS ALZ when the APOE region is excluded, possibly due to insufficient power from small GWAS sizes in diverse populations.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detected an increment in both the strength of association with AD risk and predictive performance for all non-European populations when compared to PRS EUR. No impact observed in European ancestry populations (Fig. 5, Supplementary Fig. 14, Supplementary Table 10).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Assessment of genetic predisposition to Alzheimer's Disease leveraging the multiancestry genetic variability within the APOE region through cross-ancestry Bayesian polygenic modeling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Alzheimer's Disease risk assessment in multiancestry populations (African American, Latin American, East Asian) with the crucial inclusion of the APOE region in cross-ancestry PRS models.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Significantly improves genetic risk prediction and association with Alzheimer's Disease in non-European populations when the APOE region is included, highlighting the region's importance for cross-ancestry AD genetics.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: PGS ALZ / PRS COMB (AD diagnostic specificity)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genetic Risk Score Association with diagnostic specificity

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The association between PGS ALZ / PRS COMB and AD risk weakened as the diagnosis was broadened to dementia in all multiancestry populations studied (Fig. 6 and Supplementary Table 11).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Captures genetic information specific to Alzheimer's Disease, distinguishing it from broader dementia diagnoses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Evaluation of polygenic score performance for Alzheimer's Disease risk across different diagnostic specificities (AD vs. general dementia) in multiancestry populations.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates that the genetic risk captured by PGS/PRS is primarily related to Alzheimer's Disease, and that the quality and specificity of clinical diagnosis are crucial for accurate association measurement.
